title: Burst-Forward Credits & SLA-Overflow: experiment for swapable reserved lanes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run an experiment to evaluate a new commercial construct: Burst-Forward Credits paired with an SLA-Overflow fallback lane. The idea is to let customers convert a portion of their reserved GPU commit into a bank of burst-forward credits that can be consumed in spikes, with an automated SLA-Overflow policy that routes excess traffic to a lower-cost best-effort pool when reserved capacity is exhausted. This ticket defines variants, contract language, pricing levers, and telemetry needed to assess economic and reliability trade-offs.
hypothesis: If we offer a modest fraction of reserved capacity as burst-forward credits with an explicit SLA-Overflow fallback, teams will prefer smaller base commits and use bursts for realistic traffic spikes, increasing conversions from trial to paid dedicated while keeping unit economics neutral or improved.
success_metrics: Increase in new dedicated commitments by 12% within 90 days of offering
Average committed GPU-hours per customer decreases <=10% while effective billed hours (committed + burst) increases by >=8%
SLO breach rate for customers in SLA-Overflow remains <2% during experiment windows
Net revenue per committed unit is non-decreasing relative to baseline
experiments: Variant A: 10% of commit converted to burst-forward credits, price multiplier 1.0, SLA-Overflow routes to best-effort pool with 500ms added latency SLO
Variant B: 20% credits, price multiplier 1.05, SLA-Overflow priority queue with preemptible GPUS and 1s tail latency SLO
Variant C: 10% credits + optional buyback clause for credits at 50% of list price at annual renewal
contract_changes: Add clause: definition of Burst-Forward Credits, non-refundable except as specified in buyback option
Add SLA-Overflow appendix: describes latency/availability expectations for overflow routing and customer remedies limited to credits
Add operational clause: automatic overflow routing logic and customer opt-out flow
Security addendum: Overflow routing will not send requests outside customer-designated regions and will respect VPC/private deployment constraints
ops_requirements: Telemetry: per-customer committed vs burst consumption, burst credit burn rate, overflow routing events and latency histograms
Quota policing: enforce per-tenant burst ceilings and backpressure signals to SDKs/routers
Billing: invoice line item for burst consumption and periodic reconciliation for buyback option
Console: display burst credit balance, forecast burn rate, and predicted exhaustion date
risks: Customers may game bursts and run steady-state load on burst lanes, causing capacity imbalance
SLA-Overflow could increase tail latency for mixed-tenancy pools if not properly isolated
Accounting complexity: credits accounting and buyback reconciliations add ops overhead
Legal: new contract language may require redline cycles with enterprise customers
